## Reproduction

The agent's work, under your direction. Keep all code visible.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
#| label: load
library(readxl)

data_dir <- "partB_panrivers/data"

# Experiment 3 only (sheet names per the archive details file)
preds_raw <- read_excel(
  file.path(data_dir, "Pan & Rivers (2022) - KUPE Globally Differentiated Predictions Data.xlsx"),
  sheet = "kupe3gpredsrfile"
)
crit_raw <- read_excel(
  file.path(data_dir, "Pan & Rivers (2022) - KUPE Criterial Test Data.xlsx"),
  sheet = "kupe3finaltest"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: preprocess
# Subject-level data: one row per subject x practice condition x cycle.
# Predictions code the condition as "Pretest"/"Read"; the criterial test as "Pretested"/"Read".
preds <- preds_raw |>
  mutate(COND = recode(COND, Pretest = "Pretested"))

# Sanity checks: N = 52, balanced 2 x 2 within-subject design, no missing values
stopifnot(
  n_distinct(preds$SUBJ) == 52,
  n_distinct(crit_raw$SUBJ) == 52,
  nrow(preds) == 52 * 4,
  nrow(crit_raw) == 52 * 4,
  !anyNA(preds), !anyNA(crit_raw)
)

# Wide format: one column per condition x cycle cell
preds_wide <- preds |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = SUBJ, names_from = c(COND, CYCLE), values_from = PREDICTION)
crit_wide <- crit_raw |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = SUBJ, names_from = c(COND, CYCLE), values_from = SCORE)
```

```{r}
#| label: analysis
# In a 2 x 2 fully within-subject design every effect has 1 numerator df, so the
# repeated-measures ANOVA F for an effect equals the squared one-sample t on the
# per-subject contrast for that effect (F = t^2, same p, same df).
# Partial eta squared = F * df1 / (F * df1 + df2) = t^2 / (t^2 + df2).
contrast_F <- function(x) {
  tt <- t.test(x)
  df2 <- unname(tt$parameter)
  F <- unname(tt$statistic)^2
  tibble(F = F, df1 = 1, df2 = df2, p = tt$p.value, np2 = F / (F + df2))
}

# Outcome 1: cycle x practice condition interaction on predictions
# (Pretested - Read) in cycle TWO minus the same difference in cycle ONE
out1 <- contrast_F(with(preds_wide,
  (Pretested_TWO - Read_TWO) - (Pretested_ONE - Read_ONE)))

# Outcome 2: main effect of cycle on predictions (TWO - ONE, averaged over conditions)
out2 <- contrast_F(with(preds_wide,
  (Pretested_TWO + Read_TWO) / 2 - (Pretested_ONE + Read_ONE) / 2))

# Outcomes 3 and 4: criterial test, pretested vs read, paired t-test within each cycle
paired_t <- function(pretested, read) {
  diffs <- pretested - read
  tt <- t.test(pretested, read, paired = TRUE)
  tibble(t = unname(tt$statistic), df = unname(tt$parameter),
         p = tt$p.value, d = mean(diffs) / sd(diffs))   # d = mean diff / SD of diffs
}
out3 <- paired_t(crit_wide$Pretested_ONE, crit_wide$Read_ONE)
out4 <- paired_t(crit_wide$Pretested_TWO, crit_wide$Read_TWO)
```

```{r}
#| label: results
# Reproduced values next to the paper values
results <- tribble(
  ~outcome, ~statistic, ~paper, ~reproduced,
  "1. Cycle x condition interaction (predictions)", "F(1, 51)", 10.92, out1$F,
  "1. Cycle x condition interaction (predictions)", "p",         0.0017, out1$p,
  "1. Cycle x condition interaction (predictions)", "partial eta^2", 0.18, out1$np2,
  "2. Main effect of cycle (predictions)",          "F(1, 51)", 8.83, out2$F,
  "2. Main effect of cycle (predictions)",          "p",         0.0045, out2$p,
  "2. Main effect of cycle (predictions)",          "partial eta^2", 0.15, out2$np2,
  "3. Criterial test, cycle 1",                     "t(51)",     6.67, out3$t,
  "3. Criterial test, cycle 1",                     "p",         NA, out3$p,   # paper: p < .00001
  "3. Criterial test, cycle 1",                     "d",         0.93, out3$d,
  "4. Criterial test, cycle 2",                     "t(51)",     5.99, out4$t,
  "4. Criterial test, cycle 2",                     "p",         NA, out4$p,   # paper: p < .0001
  "4. Criterial test, cycle 2",                     "d",         0.83, out4$d
)

knitr::kable(results, digits = c(NA, NA, 4, 6),
             col.names = c("Target outcome", "Statistic", "Paper", "Reproduced"))
```

## Checker's verdict

Filled in by you, not the agent.

| # | Paper value | Reproduced value | Verdict (exact / minor / major / not reproducible) | Reason for discrepancy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | F(1, 51) = 10.92, p = .0017, ηp² = .18 | F(1, 51) = 10.922, p = .001743, ηp² = .1764 | exact | All values agree after rounding. |
| 2 | F(1, 51) = 8.83, p = .0045, ηp² = .15 | F(1, 51) = 8.833, p = .004506, ηp² = .1476 | exact | All values agree after rounding. |
| 3 | t(51) = 6.67, p < .00001, d = 0.93 | t(51) = 6.673, p ≈ 1.8e-8, d = 0.925 | exact | All values agree after rounding. |
| 4 | t(51) = 5.99, p < .0001, d = 0.83 | t(51) = 5.993, p ≈ 2.1e-7, d = 0.831 | exact | All values agree after rounding. |

Agent's own claim about success, and whether it was right:

The agent said it reproduced all four outcomes in Python. I checked this by running the R code and rendering the report in Quarto. The results matched the original paper after rounding. The agent wrote the R code but did not run it; the R code ran when I rendered the report.

## Time

- Your time (hours): 30 minutes (0.50 hours)
- Agent wall-clock time (hours): 5 minutes (0.08 hours)
- Stopped at the 4-hour cap? What remained: No. When the agent finished, I still needed to render the report to see the R code.

## Assessment

Is the primary result analytically reproducible? What would have made this take 30 minutes?

Yes, the results are reproducible. I ran the R code in the report and got the same results as the paper at the precision it reported. My part took 30 minutes. Connecting the folder before the first prompt would have saved some time. The authors provided everything I needed.

## AI documentation

- Agent and interface (e.g., Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor): Claude desktop app (Cowork).
- Model and version, if the tool reports it: Claude Sonnet 5.5.
- Context you gave it (files, instructions, any context file): I gave Claude access to the folder with `partB_check_report.qmd` and `partB_panrivers/data`. - Initial prompt: Reproduce the four target outcomes in partB_check_report.qmd (Pan & Rivers 2023, Experiment 3) using the data in partB_panrivers/data. Write the analysis code in the Reproduction section of partB_check_report.qmd (R code chunks, all code visible), and report each reproduced value as a number next to the paper value. Do not edit the target outcomes, the materials inventory, the checker's verdict, Time, Assessment or AI documentation sections: those are mine. If R or Quarto is not available to you, write the R code anyway, verify the numbers with Python, and tell me clearly what you ran and what you did not run. Do not look at files outside this folder.
- Number of times you intervened, and the most important intervention: I intervened once after my first prompt. I connected the folder and wrote “Try now.” Then the agent could access the files and start the analysis.
